subject: SLA review: 2027-05-29 checkout availability blip and remedy ask
messages:

Subject: Re: SLA review: 2027-05-29 checkout availability blip and remedy ask

Hi Neha,

We observed a burst of 503s on our checkout endpoint during our peak evening window on 2027-05-29 between ~22:01 and 22:13 UTC. This impacted our conversion flow for ~12 minutes and maps to ~8% drop in completion for that minute bucket on our side (we've attached a short error histogram).

Quick summary:
- Region: us-west-2 (tenant pinned to hosted endpoint)
- Window we care about: 2027-05-29T22:01:00Z -> 2027-05-29T22:13:00Z
- User-facing symptom: intermittent 503 responses on POST /v1/checkout/complete
- Business impact: estimated ~$14k lost GMV in that 12-minute window

Can you confirm whether this meets Redwood's SLA eligibility for availability credits and what evidence you need from our side? We need an expected timeline for a post-incident report — our security/compliance and finance teams are asking for decisional guidance this week.

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Sullivan
Head of Ops, Streamline Commerce
megan.sullivan@streamline.com

Subject: Re: SLA review: 2027-05-29 checkout availability blip and remedy ask

Hi Megan — thanks for flagging and for the histogram. I'm sorry for the disruption. I started a ticket and asked infra to pull the traces and autoscaler logs for the window you referenced.

Initial notes from our telemetry:
- We see a high spike in request rejections (503) from the tenant's backend between 22:01:38Z and 22:12:19Z.
- There are correlated KV cache eviction events and a transient rise in preemption signals in the same shard group.
- The serving cluster had a rolling firmware upgrade in progress; we observed one node briefly drop and rejoin around 22:07Z which increased tail latencies.

To validate eligibility for an SLA credit we need:
1) Your acceptance of our evidence pull (we will provide a redacted trace bundle).
2) Any customer-side retry/ingestion logs you can share for the same window (a small sample is sufficient).

Attaching: raw-traces-20270529.zip (contains span-level traces and 1s-sampled logs). Also attaching a small kv-eviction-snippet.txt that highlights the eviction markers.

Next steps I propose:
- Today: confirm receipt and provide any additional traces from your side.
- <48 hours: Redwood infra will produce a tentative eligibility calc and a proposed credit amount with an explanation of the apportionment method.
- 10 business days: full post-incident report (scope, RCA, mitigations, and follow-up actions).

If you prefer an accelerated cadence for compliance, we can prioritize a preliminary RCAsandbox within 72 hours — it will be higher-level but faster.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Megan Sullivan <megan.sullivan@streamline.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2027 19:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: SLA review: 2027-05-29 checkout availability blip and remedy ask

Thanks for the bundle — I pulled the relevant spans. A short technical readout:

What happened (short):
- The tenant's traffic hit a shard that experienced a double eviction of cached prefixes due to a rare interaction between our asynchronous prefix cache reclamation and a rolling node rejoin. That reclamation led to a burst of cache-miss amplification causing request queueing. The autoscaler briefly engaged a circuit-breaker to protect the serving node, resulting in 503s for new connections until warmup completed.

Why this is unusual:
- Normally our autoscaler allows a short warmup and routes to healthy nodes; the combination of mesh-level rejoin plus near-simultaneous cache eviction amplified the hit ratio drop and exceeded the SLO guard.

Preliminary eligibility calc:
- Window of confirmed service unavailability: 2027-05-29T22:03:00Z -> 2027-05-29T22:11:00Z (8 minutes where error rate > threshold).
- Per the contract's SLA clause 4.2, we pro-rate credit by percentage of downtime in the month. For the 8-minute window that maps to a 0.56% uptime delta for May (30-day month) -> eligible credit = monthly invoice * 0.0056, capped per the SLA.

Recommended remedial package (to make this different from a pure credit):
1) Credit: provisional prorated credit (we'll calculate once finance confirms invoice amount).
2) Engineering warmup: a free 1-week dedicated warmup pool for your highest-traffic tenant routes (to reduce cold-path exposure).
3) Postmortem + action items: prioritize fixes to asynchronous cache reclamation path and adjust autoscaler slack for your tenant class.

I'll put this into a short PDF with the exact math — happy to walk through the numbers with your finance lead.

Diego Fernandez
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLA review: 2027-05-29 checkout availability blip and remedy ask

Hi Megan — following up with an agreed path. Thanks for the quick reports and the histogram. To be explicit:

1) Evidence and timeline
- Redwood confirms an availability anomaly that overlaps your reported window. Our conservative validated window is 2027-05-29T22:03:00Z -> 2027-05-29T22:11:00Z. We will include the sampled traces and autoscaler logs in the postmortem.

2) Credit eligibility and calculation
- We will provisionally calculate the prorated credit as described by Diego (0.56% of monthly invoice for May). Final credit requires your May invoice reference — please confirm the invoice number or a contact at your billing team and we will run final math.

3) Compensation & remediation
- Provisional credit (subject to final invoice confirmation).
- One-week complimentary dedicated warmup pool for your primary checkout routes (no cost).
- Engineering action items: a scheduled fix to the async cache reclamation in the next patch cycle; a short-term autoscaler config change to increase warmup slack for high-throughput tenants.

4) Post-incident schedule
- Preliminary eligibility calc and draft credit amount: within 48 hours (Mon 2027-05-31 EOD PT).
- Full postmortem with root cause, mitigations, and ETA for code fix: within 10 business days (target: 2027-06-14).

5) Accept/reject evidence pull
- Please reply with authorization to include your tenant id in our internal trace bundle. If you want additional redaction we can do field-level masking.

If that works for you I will open the formal SLA claim and route to finance + engineering.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
